text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. speaker: Doctor

DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency) with hemarthrosis of the right knee.

*Explanation of the reasoning leading to this immediate conclusion:* The patient is a young male (18 months) presenting with spontaneous, painless, non-traumatic knee swelling (hemarthrosis) and a specific family history of similar issues on the maternal side (X-linked recessive inheritance pattern). This clinical picture is classic for a bleeding disorder like Hemophilia A, rather than an inflammatory or degenerative joint disease. Further confirmatory testing would include Factor VIII activity levels and a complete blood count, but the diagnosis is strongly supported by the current presentation and history.
